text:
kevin: Hey team, seeing a sharp spike of pod restarts in serving-runtime in us-west-2. Multiple pods reporting CUDA illegal memory access and OOMs. Not sure if this is regression from the latest kernel or the recent model rollout. tagging @oncall.

anya: @kevin can you paste the container logs? do we have dmesg / kernel traces yet? :eyes:

kevin: Pasting trimmed logs below (from one of the crashed pods):
```
[2024-06-12T22:04:12Z] serving-runtime[pid=2345]: cudaStreamSynchronize -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
[2024-06-12T22:04:12Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (serving-runtime) score 987
[2024-06-12T22:04:13Z] nvidia: 0x7fffa1b2c3d4 Illegal memory access at address 0x0000deadbeef
```

jin: I also pulled dmesg from the host node - looks like repeated pagewalk faults: "GPU: dev-pte: page table walk returned invalid entry". Repro window around 22:03-22:10UTC.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-20240612-1193 - high pod restart rate (serving-runtime) - Severity: P2 - oncall: @anya

anya: I'm on it. Initial triage: node-level or container-level? can we confirm if the same GPU shows faults across multiple containers (i.e., kernel vs per-process)?

kevin: Two nodes (node-uw2-a and node-uw2-b) show the illegal access. Each had multiple containers crash but with different PIDs. suggests something kernel-level (driver / smmu / pagewalk) rather than single model binary.

taylor: Noted. Rolling back yesterday's runtime patch is an option but that would be disruptive. Quick mitigations: cordon one affected node, drain to repro-isolated hosts, enable fallback model variant (cpu-safe) for live traffic, scale down requests to the cluster. Thoughts?

sre-sasha: Agree with cordon+drain on most affected nodes. Also put serving runtime into canary: reduce replica count to 1 per node for a short window to see if rate affects repro (maybe KV cache eviction combined with concurrent GC triggers misaligned pointer read).

kevin: Running these commands now: 
```
kubectl cordon node-uw2-a
kubectl drain node-uw2-a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl scale deployment/serving-runtime -n prod --replicas=6
```

ops-bot: rollout:deployment/serving-runtime started by kevin (reason: incident mitigation)

jin: quick check: nvidia-smi on node-uw2-b shows no ECC errors but GPU memory usage is high and there are runaway allocs during spikes. Collecting GPU coredumps.

anya: Customer impact? any requests failing externally? SLOs?

kevin: Our metrics show a ~12% 5xx spike for text-generation endpoints over the last 10min. Most failures are internal 500s from worker restarts, not auth or network. Customers on Dedicated might see latency blips, hosted API has retries.

taylor: I'll draft a short customer notice: "We are investigating a GPU runtime issue causing intermittent request failures in us-west-2. Some requests may retry or experience increased latency. Engineers are cordoning nodes and rolling mitigations." Anyone object?

sre-sasha: go ahead, include ETA: we'll update every 30min. Add note recommending retry/backoff from client side.

kevin: Investigation update: reproduced locally with a stress test that does long-context generation + KV cache thrash. It seems a race between continuous batching and KV cache eviction where a freed pointer is being used in the next micro-batch on the same GPU. Not 100% sure yet.

jin: Posting a stack snippet from the runtime tracer (obfuscated):
```
serving_runtime::kv_cache::evict_chunk at kv_cache.rs:412
serving_runtime::batch::commit at batch.rs:198
gpu_driver::launch_kernel at kernel.cu:87  // returns CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
```

anya: If that's the case, a conservative quick fix is to disable prefix/KV caching globally or serialise cache eviction with batch commits. Can we toggle the flag remotely?

kevin: Yes we have a feature flag: `KV_CACHE_CONCURRENT_EVICTION=true` in the config map. I'm issuing a patch to set it to false (rollout to canary first).

ops-bot: configmap/serving-config updated by kevin - rolling restart scheduled

taylor: Also consider forcing the runtime to use host-pinned memory for KV buffers as a temporary workaround (even though it increases latency). That may avoid bad GPU pointer aliasing.

jin: GPU coredump analysis: GPU VA showed entries pointing to stale SMMU mappings on the host. Might be a kernel/driver interaction under specific seq lengths. Opening bug with NV driver team with trace.

anya: Action items:
- kevin: roll the KV cache flag to canary (1 node) and monitor 5xxs and CUDA errors (30m)
- jin: collect and upload GPU coredumps + dmesg + SMMU traces to the ticket
- taylor: publish customer notice and coordinate with CS for any high-value accounts
- sasha: prepare rollback plan for runtime v2.3.1 if mitigation fails

kevin: Canary applied to node-uw2-c (replica pinned). initial logs show decreased illegal memory errors - two crashes in last 15m vs 12 previously. continuing to monitor.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: #INC-20240612-1193 - mitigation in progress (KV cache concurrency disabled on canary). severity remains P2.

taylor: Posted the customer notice: "Investigating GPU runtime instability in us-west-2 causing intermittent generation failures; mitigation deployed to a small canary. We will update in 30 minutes." pinging CS.

jin: NV ticket opened (ref NV-4382) with attached traces and timestamps. they asked for device kernel logs; I'm uploading now.

anya: If canary holds for 30m, we'll roll to remaining nodes and gradually restore traffic. If failures persist after rollback/flag toggle, escalate to emergency kernel rollback and consider temporarily shifting serving to Dedicated fallback instances in a different region.

kevin: 30m check-in: canary good. error rate dropped to baseline. scaling rollout to remaining pods now (rolling restart).

ops-bot: rollout:deployment/serving-runtime completed for canary subset

sre-sasha: once rollout finishes, let's keep enhanced tracing enabled for 24h and add alert to detect repeat of the illegal address pattern (match stack + nv error). Also add a synthetic test that runs the KV cache stress scenario nightly.

taylor: Thanks everyone. I'll prepare the post-incident summary template and list next steps (driver bug follow-up, code fix to remove race, test harness to catch this).

kevin: Closing note: root cause suspected race between KV cache eviction and batch commit leading to stale GPU pointers. Temporary mitigation applied by serialising eviction. NV driver team engaged. I'll file a PR with the guarded change tomorrow. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: #INC-20240612-1193 - mitigation verified after rollout; severity downgraded. Final postmortem to follow.
